stage.name: Sakaide to Sanuki
stage.theme: The longest day of the forty, and the most crowded
stage.narrative: 59.6 km, the longest day of the forty this cut made, and it is long for an absence: nothing is mapped as a place to stay for 86.1 km, and this day is 59.6 of that stretch. No town falls in it either, until the one it ends at. What the day is not is empty. More places stand on this one day than on any other of the six, and the longest run with nothing mapped on it is only 4.2 km. Seven temples come among them — Tennō-ji, Sanuki Kokubun-ji, Shiromine-ji, Negoro-ji, Ichinomiya-ji, Yashima-ji and Yakuri-ji — and thirty-one places to eat. Everything except somewhere to stop.
stage.closing: The busiest day in Sanuki and the longest of the forty, and those are one fact: nothing mapped on it is a place to sleep. How much of what you carry is decided by what someone wrote down?
warnings: 59.6 km, the longest day on the circuit. OpenStreetMap records no named accommodation or town on the walked line between Sakaide and Sanuki, so the rule had nowhere nearer to stop. Carry water and food for the whole distance, or break the day at a place off the line.
